bluf: Ignite Visibility is a San Diego search and performance agency of 700+ specialists that sells scale to enterprise, franchise and multi location brands under a proprietary AI platform, Rallio AI. The record shows it leading with SEO and local, adding AI SEO, digital PR for AI citations and CRO, and running 200 Google ads and 20+ LinkedIn ads of its own. It lists no moves, no case studies and one client, a testimonial. A rival should know the Horus read is Neutral at 5, most exposed to the hollowing of the agency middle through SEO, and that two sold lines, paid social and CRO, fail their own house tests.
doing:
The positioning line reads: award winning agency built for enterprise, franchise and multi location growth, pairing 700+ specialists with its proprietary Rallio AI marketing platform. In plain words: a large search shop selling headcount plus software to brands with many locations. The headline claim is trust signals rather than results: Top 1% Google Premier Partner and a 4.8 of 5 rating across 173 Clutch reviews.

The services list adds Display Advertising, Influencer Marketing, Email & SMS Marketing, Website Development and Franchise Marketing to the search, PR, paid and CRO lines. The lead lines at 3 are Local (the About page says engineered for enterprise, franchise and multi location growth, 15,000+ client locations, a franchise SEO line) and SEO (the meta leads with SEO; the SEO page cites 20+ years of ROI; the agency made SEO: The Movie). Core lines at 2 are AI Automation / Agents (Powered by Rallio AI, running strategy, execution and attribution on one platform), AI Search / GEO (an AI SEO page with a retrievability and entity mapping framework that claims 458% AI visibility growth), CRO, Content & Digital PR (journalist outreach and link earning tied to AI citation goals), Paid Search (PPC; 196 own Google ads per the note) and Paid Social (Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and LinkedIn service pages). Proprietary names: Rallio AI and RevIntel. The one partner listed is Google Premier Partner (Top 1%).

The AI posture is platform branding: the agency is powered by Rallio AI, and it sells AI SEO, digital PR for AI citations and ChatGPT ads know how, yet Data & Measurement scores 1 for a platform that claims attribution.

The record lists no dated moves, no news items, no case studies and no jobs. Pricing signals: no prices published, free audits and proposals, and a promise of contract flexibility. Conspicuously absent for a 700+ person agency: a single described client engagement, and any measurement line above 1.
clients:
The Radar files the client type as enterprise, the home market as the US with offices in San Diego, Irvine, New York and Orlando, and the verticals as Franchises & multi-location, Dental, Healthcare, Home services (HVAC, electrical), Automotive, Financial services, Insurance, Ecommerce, B2B and Fitness brands. The needs read counts 1 client, observed 0, named only 1: Universal Funding Corporation, present as a testimonial on the services page with nothing about the work, so its need is inferred from the sold mix, search and paid media for lead generation, and the sentence says so.

The mix read is empty because no need was observed, and no client is shared with another tracked agency. The clients page sits in the source list, yet no logo, case study or press release survived into the record: the 15,000+ locations claim has no named client behind it, and the one name is a testimonial. The whole book is names only (1 of 1).

The verticals and the ad copy point the same way: the Google ad samples sell franchise development and franchise lead generation, and the LinkedIn samples talk to brands running 50, 500 or 5,000 locations and warn that waiting one day to respond to leads reduces conversion.

What the base needs next: KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation) is its tailwind, so it is likely, with moderate confidence, that its franchise and dental accounts are sold AI SEO and citation focused digital PR on top of local search; KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out) is its headwind through SEO, so it is a roughly even chance that the SEO retainers behind those accounts are repriced within the edition. With no client on record, both are judgments about the sold mix, not the book.
house: Say and do: 4 of 6 tested lines are practised on its own house. AI Search / GEO is corroborated: it publishes llms.txt and 8 AI topic URLs sit in its sitemap. Paid search is corroborated: 200 Google ads in the Transparency Center, 53 in the last 30 days, last shown 27 September 2026; one sample reads Franchise Development Agency, Find Qualified Franchisees. LinkedIn advertising is corroborated: 20+ ads as a floor, 8 company page and 12 thought leader ads by agency staff. Paid social is contradicted: it sells paid social and runs no social ad pixel on its own site. CRO is contradicted: it sells CRO and no testing tool was detected on its homepage. Publishing cadence is marked corroborated, yet the figures are near idle: 1 URL updated in 90 days and 2 in 365 from a sitemap of 1,515. The tag stack is GTM and Axeptio on WordPress; no test tools or ABM stack are listed.
market:

It is best placed for KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation, net 0.175), driven by AI Search / GEO and Content & Digital PR, and for KJ2 (ads inside AI answers scale faster than any channel before them, net 0.14). It is most exposed to KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out, net -0.108) through SEO and Paid Search. Best fit is The Walled Oasis at 32/100. The read has it making only P2 (feeds and entities), partial on P1, P3, P4, P6, P7 and P8, and unknown on P5.

The Monsoon read scores 52.6, Breeze band: migration 55.1 against displacement 50.1, with SEO (11) and Local (10) carrying the most movable hours. The work would go 65% to South and Southeast Asia and 25% to Latin America. No hub office and no onshore claim are listed, so the footprint is inferred; the enterprise client type counts against displacement.
openings:
Lead with the empty book. An agency of 700+ people shows one client on record, a testimonial, and no case study; a rival with written franchise or dental cases can ask prospects to name a published result. Very likely, high confidence, this lands; the falsifier is a case study page with named clients and figures under ignitevisibility.com.

Second, the two contradictions: it sells paid social with no social pixel, and CRO with no testing tool on its homepage. A rival whose house passes both puts the gap on one slide; likely.

Third, AI SEO without the audit: it claims 458% AI visibility growth but the read finds no audited AI visibility product (P1 partial), so a rival with citation share and a scorecard leads with the number. Fourth, paid media without inputs: no first party data, creative volume or measurement depth shows (P4 partial) and Data & Measurement scores 1 under a platform claiming attribution; the inputs are the pitch against it. Fifth, local without LSAs: no LSA or Sponsored Places work shows (P3 partial), so the franchise accounts are contestable by whoever runs them; likely, moderate confidence. No public pricing (P5 unknown) leaves room for an outcome priced offer.
